title: Application of machine learning to monster level prediction in tabletop RPG game design
abstract: arXiv:2607.09196v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Designing balanced adversaries is a central but labor-intensive task in tabletop role-playing game (TTRPG) development. In systems such as Pathfinder, each monster is described by many numerical attributes that jointly determine its power, summarized as an ordinal level. We investigate whether machine learning can support designers by predicting this level from a monster's attributes, framing the task as tabular ordinal regression. We introduce what is, to our knowledge, the first dataset built specifically for TTRPG monster-level prediction, derived from publicly available Pathfinder Second Edition data. Using it, we compare classical regression models with rounding schemes, dedicated tabular ordinal regression algorithms, and neural networks with ordinal-aware losses. tldr: 本研究首次构建了基于Pathfinder第二版数据的TTRPG怪物等级预测数据集，并系统比较了多种机器学习方法，为游戏设计中的对手平衡提供了自动化支持。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the first dataset for TTRPG monster level prediction from Pathfinder 2E data, systematically comparing machine learning methods to automate adversary balancing in game design.
